affectedPublicSurfaces: STOP REASONS ON THE RUN LIST AND THE EVENT STREAM. `services/agent_runs/listing.py::RunListItem` exposes `stop_reason: str | None` on `GET /demo/runs`, and the `workflow.completed`/`workflow.failed` payloads carry it on the SSE stream at `GET /demo/runs/{run_id}/events`. Every value added here can appear on a seller's screen from the first run after cutover, so this is a vocabulary change on a live surface, not an internal enum.

THREE MIRRORS OF ONE VOCABULARY, all of which must move together: `services/agent/status.py::StopReason` (sixteen members today) plus its TOTAL `STOP_REASON_TO_STATUS` map; the Postgres CHECK `ck_workflow_runs_stop_reason`, whose sixteen-value IN-list is declared BOTH in `models.py::WorkflowRun.__table_args__` and in a migration; and `packages/contracts/src/agent-events.ts`'s `STOP_REASONS` const array backing `export type StopReason`, together with the twelve-member `WORKFLOW_FAILED_STOP_REASON_TO_STATUS` table that mirrors the failure-class subset.

CONTRADICTION 1 — `confirmation_expired` IS NOT NEW. The issue lists it among the causes to add, but `StopReason.CONFIRMATION_EXPIRED = "confirmation_expired"` already exists, is already in the CHECK, is already in the TypeScript array, and already maps to `WorkflowRunStatus.CANCELLED`. The issue's rule 'each maps to `completed` except the two vendor/expiry failures' would silently REMAP an existing reason from `cancelled` to `completed` — a semantic regression on live data that the totality test would happily accept. Leave its mapping exactly as it is and say so in the PR. `external_wait_expired` is likewise already added by #1706 and must not be re-declared. So the issue's twenty-one names are NINETEEN additions, which is what spec §8.1 P0-9's '~20 new causes' actually means.

CONTRADICTION 2 — 'the TS union equals the backend enum' IS ASSERTED BY NOTHING TODAY. `tests/unit/test_agent_events_contract.py` is the repo's dual-language test (it shells out to `node -e` and `require("typescript")` against `packages/contracts`), but its mapping assertion is `test_workflow_failed_stop_reason_to_status_mapping_matches_python_for_all_twelve_members` — the twelve-member FAILURE subset only. Nothing anywhere compares the full sixteen-member `STOP_REASONS` to the Python `StopReason`. Worse, `packages/contracts/src/__tests__/agent-events.test.ts` asserts `expect(STOP_REASONS).toHaveLength(13)` against an array that already holds sixteen — that vitest assertion is RED today and `.github/workflows/pr.yml` never runs vitest for `packages/contracts`, which is why it has gone unnoticed. Acceptance criterion 1 therefore requires ADDING the full-union equality assertion (and fixing or deliberately deleting the stale length assertion), not extending one that exists.

THE TERMINAL TOOL'S SIGNATURE. `services/agent/tools/terminal.py` (behind `TERMINAL_TOOL_HANDLERS`) exposes `conclude_without_changes`, the one terminal tool named in `OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_TERMINATION_POLICY.terminal_tools`. It gains a `cause` argument constrained to this vocabulary; an unknown cause is refused. Because the tool's `input_model` is part of the composed prompt's tool block, a shape change here is visible to the playbook-consistency gate — expect it to fire and treat that as the gate working.

SELLER COPY, in Vietnamese, for every cause. Each new cause needs a completion line through the existing outbound banned-pattern guard (`packages/contracts/seller-copy-banned-patterns.json`, `tests/unit/test_agent_banned_patterns_contract.py`, `tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_copy_governance_gate.py`): second person, no English, no internal identifiers, no projected impact magnitudes, no causal claims (S-NFR-4).

The `String(32)` ceiling on `workflow_runs.stop_reason` binds every name. The longest proposed is `not_received_by_needed_date` (27); `expired_stock_remaining` (23) and `vendor_partial_failure` (22) also fit. Assert the ceiling in the test rather than trusting the count.

A widened IN-list accepts every value it accepted before, so the previous release keeps writing and reading `workflow_runs` unchanged — it simply never emits the new causes. No column is added, dropped, renamed or retyped; no backfill, no NOT NULL, and `workflow_runs.stop_reason` stays `String(32)` (assert the longest new name, `not_received_by_needed_date` at 27 characters, against that width rather than counting by eye). The same constraint text also lives in `models.py::WorkflowRun.__table_args__` and must move in the SAME commit or the schema-parity test finds the drift after the fact. Two names in the issue's list are NOT additions and must not be re-declared: `confirmation_expired` already exists and maps to `cancelled`; `external_wait_expired` was added by #1706. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. The vocabulary stays at sixteen reasons, none of the causes ADR-090–093 name exist, and a run that ends for a workflow-specific reason keeps borrowing `final_response` or `concluded_without_changes` — indistinguishable end states, which is the pre-existing defect. Nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release FIRST and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker: the previous code neither writes nor recognises the new causes, so it runs correctly against the widened CHECK and needs no downgrade — a historical row carrying `goal_met` is simply a string it does not enumerate, and `RunListItem.stop_reason` is a plain `str | None` on the way out. Only if the schema must ALSO be reverted, `alembic downgrade -1` narrows the CHECK back, and that downgrade MUST FAIL LOUDLY with an explicit named error, never silently delete or coerce a row, when ANY `workflow_runs` row carries one of the new causes — and, when #1706's or #1701's schema is being reverted in the same operation, when any row sits in `waiting_external` or carries a non-product `subject_type` or a NULL `product_id`. Both refusals are asserted pre-merge. Order: previous code first, downgrade second, so no live process is mid-write against a constraint being narrowed. The honest caveat to state in the PR: a client with an exhaustive switch over the TypeScript union that has already shipped will meet an unknown cause after a partial rollback — the seller copy must degrade to a neutral Vietnamese completion line, never to a blank or to the raw identifier.
